summary: iter118q — Zelle → Stripe Connect Express backend migration verified end-to-end. All 13 backend tests pass (fee split math, new /api/trainer/connect/status shape, /api/trainer/connect/account-link Stripe-restriction forwarding, /api/admin/trainers/connect-status listing + ordering, legacy /api/trainer/request-payout returning 410, mark_session_eligible_for_release T+24h scheduling, release_due_transfers awaiting-onboarding path, webhook _handle_account_updated + _handle_payout_paid, and migration script idempotency).
critical_code_review_comments: connect_routes.get_connect_status hits Stripe (Balance.retrieve + Payout.list) on every /status call — cache or debounce (e.g., 30s) to keep the trainer Earnings tab snappy and reduce Stripe API pressure.

release_due_transfers claims a row atomically with transferState IN ['pending','retry'], but rows the worker itself parked as 'awaiting-onboarding' will NEVER be re-picked (they don't match the claim filter on a later tick). Add 'awaiting-onboarding' to the claim IN-list so trainers who finish onboarding late get their held funds released automatically.

POST /api/trainer/connect/account-link — the current live Stripe account is rejecting new Express account creation ('temporarily restricted'). This is a Stripe-side dashboard config issue, not a code bug, and the endpoint correctly surfaces the Stripe error. Flag with the ops team to lift the Stripe restriction before public rollout.

compute_platform_and_trainer_split uses banker's rounding via round(); for odd cent prices the trainer could lose a cent to the platform. Consider math.floor for the platform share to keep the trainer's cut deterministic and slightly favorable.

success_rate.frontend: n/a — frontend is Expo React Native, out of scope

seed_data_creation: No permanent seed data. Tests self-clean: TEST_*-prefixed trainer_profiles/sessions/trainer_payouts rows are deleted in finally blocks. The connect-status test temporarily unsets and restores the real trainer's stripeConnectAccountId inside a try/finally.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_iter118q_stripe_connect_migration.py uses a shared asyncio event loop (_shared_loop) and rebinds deps.db to it so webhook handlers (which import deps.db module-level) work across multiple asyncio.run boundaries. Reuse the _arun helper pattern for any future direct-service async tests. The migration script scripts/migrate_zelle_to_connect.py is proven idempotent (2nd run yields 0/0/0 modified counts).
rca of the issue: n/a — no bugs found. Note: initial test failures were pytest-side (motor client stuck on a closed event loop across asyncio.run boundaries), fixed by binding one shared loop and rebinding deps.db to it. Not a product bug.
